rulings.ruling: Ruling: ambiguity and scope; i1040gi p. 90, worksheet line 1: "But don’t enter more than the amount of your state and local income taxes shown on your 2024 Schedule A, line 5d". (1) The cap at all of line 5d rather than its income tax part is the register's chosen reading, amb.2025.refund_cap_5d (owner decision D6(a), Stage 16: cap line 1 at 2024 Schedule A line 5d as printed; a refund above the income tax part is exception 4 territory, refund.exc_tax). (2) i1040gi p. 89, Line 1, Exception: "1. You received a refund in 2025 that is for a tax year other than 2024", "2. You received a refund other than an income tax refund, such as a general sales tax or real property tax refund, in 2025 of an amount deducted or credit claimed in an earlier year" and "5. You made your last payment of 2024 estimated state or local income tax in 2025". Exceptions 1 and 5 are refused by refund.not_2024 ("Is any of these refunds for a tax year other than 2024 (box 3 of Form 1099-G), or did you pay any of your 2024 state or local income tax in 2025?", reworded under BUG-0230 and now wider than exception 5), whose refusal sits on refund.taxable, the line Schedule 1 line 1 enters, so no such refund reaches line 1 on a completed return; the model saw only line 1's two refusals (exc_tax, exc_who: items 3, 4, 6 to 9). Exception 2 is outside refund.received ("State or local income tax refunds, credits or offsets") and refused by scope.schedule1 ("a refund or other recovery of an amount you deducted or took a credit for in an earlier year, other than a state or local income tax refund (for example a refund of general sales tax, real estate tax or personal property tax ...)"): scope, refusal located on the reading line. The rendered English of line 1 is unchanged; the screen wording that changed is not part of this line. Project retained.

rulings.model: The IRS says 'Multiply the number of boxes checked by $1,550 ($1,950 if your 2024 filing status was single or head of household)', but the per-box helpers are not defined in the glossary, so neither the rate nor its dependence on filing status can be confirmed. The definitions are also needed to confirm that spouse boxes for married filing separately apply only if the spouse 'had no income, isn't filing a return, and can't be claimed as a dependent', and the text given does not state the restatement's zeroing of spouse boxes for a qualifying surviving spouse.
rulings.ruling: Ruling: representation; i1040gi p. 90, worksheet line 6: "Multiply the number of boxes checked by $1,550 ($1,950 if your 2024 filing status was single or head of household)" and footnote "*If your filing status is married filing separately, you can check the boxes for your spouse only if your spouse had no income, isn’t filing a return, and can’t be claimed as a dependent on another person’s return"; p. 33, Line 12d: "Don’t check any boxes for your spouse if your filing status is head of household". Each per-box helper is refund.per_box when its box is checked and zero otherwise, and refund.per_box is labelled and encoded "$1,550 ($1,950 if your 2024 filing status was single or head of household)" (single/hoh -> refund.box_unmarried $1,950; mfj/mfs/qss -> refund.box_married $1,550), so the sum is the number of boxes times the amount; the rate is stated in the label of refund.per_box, which the restatement reaches through the per-box helpers, so the "missing" amount and status condition are one helper further down. The married filing separately condition is in the spouse questions themselves (refund.spouse_born, refund.spouse_blind: "If your 2024 filing status was married filing separately, answer yes only if your spouse also had no income, wasn't filing a return, and couldn't be claimed as a dependent on another person's return"), as the footnote says; amb.2025.refund_boxes_2024 records the status reading. The model also asks about the zero spouse boxes for a qualifying surviving spouse: the restatement zeroes them for every 2024 status other than married filing jointly or separately, as the register's chosen reading records ("a single or qualifying surviving spouse return has no spouse whose boxes it checks"; i1040gi p. 33, Line 12d, "If you or your spouse (if you are married and filing a joint return)"). The per-box helpers are defined in rendered/2025/refund.md (refund.amt_you_born and the others: the per-box amount when the box is yes, zero otherwise). Same as the archived rulings. Project retained. Each per-box helper is refund.per_box ("$1,550 ($1,950 if your 2024 filing status was single or head of household)": single/hoh -> refund.box_unmarried $1,950; mfj/mfs/qss -> refund.box_married $1,550) when its box is checked and zero otherwise, so the sum is boxes times the rate. The rate was not checkable by the model because helpers are glossed only by label (the label does state the rate). On the qualifying-surviving-spouse point (spouse boxes zero unless 2024 status MFJ or MFS): ambiguity, amb.2025.refund_boxes_2024 (chosen reading: "ask the spouse questions only when the 2024 filing status was married filing jointly or married filing separately"); the worksheet is silent on QSS, and on the 2024 Form 1040 the spouse boxes belong to a spouse on the return.
